weaknesses: The abstract does not clearly articulate the limitations of the proposed IRS method, particularly in scenarios with significant network modifications.
The paper lacks a comprehensive comparison with existing incremental certification methods beyond randomized smoothing, limiting the context of its contributions.
The experimental results do not sufficiently address the variability in performance across different architectures and datasets, which may affect generalizability.
strengths: The introduction of the Incremental Randomized Smoothing (IRS) method represents a significant advancement in the efficiency of robustness certification for deep neural networks.
The paper provides a clear theoretical foundation for the IRS approach, supported by rigorous proofs and insights into the underlying statistical principles.
Extensive empirical evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness of IRS, showcasing substantial speedups in certification times compared to baseline methods.
